subject.title: [Feature Request] Infrastructure Expansion: Time to implement Global Mirrors and Load Balancing for OpenClaw

question: Should ClawHub pursue source-owned global mirrors and health-routed load balancing now, or defer this as external/provider operations until a narrower architecture is approved?
rationale: The request changes production topology and security boundaries, and the issue does not define the provider, trust model, rollout plan, or repository-owned scope that automation could safely infer.

options.title: Scope Architecture First
options.body: Write a maintainer-owned design covering topology, trust boundaries, failover semantics, cache consistency, observability, rollout, rollback, and repo-owned changes before implementation.

options.title: Defer As External Ops
options.body: Leave this issue open or close later as out of source scope if maintainers decide mirrors/load balancing are provider administration rather than ClawHub repository work.

options.title: Split Narrow Subtasks
options.body: Keep this umbrella for product direction but track only approved subpieces, such as trusted edge headers or feed delivery, in separate issues or PRs.

recommendation.title: Scope Architecture First
recommendation.body: Write a maintainer-owned design covering topology, trust boundaries, failover semantics, cache consistency, observability, rollout, rollback, and repo-owned changes before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Patrick is the strongest current-history owner for deployment docs, routing config, and CODEOWNERS-backed security-sensitive API/deploy surfaces.
